subject.title: fix: protect SMS webhook callback quota [AI]

question: Should SMS preserve a valid signed callback after unauthenticated traffic exhausts the same account, route, and client key, or intentionally fail closed for every request on that key?
rationale: The handler cannot authenticate before doing some request work, but the proposed early limiter lets attacker-controlled traffic suppress valid delivery; selecting the permanent security-versus-availability policy requires owner intent.

options.title: Preserve authenticated delivery
options.body: Redesign pre-authentication admission so invalid traffic remains bounded without consuming the path a valid signed callback must pass, and prove the same-key sequence.

options.title: Accept fail-closed denial
options.body: Keep the early shared gate only with explicit acceptance and documentation that invalid same-key traffic can reject valid callbacks for the fixed window.

options.title: Pause this redesign
options.body: Pause or close this PR if a safe SMS-local admission scheme cannot be established without a broader generic webhook-ingress change.

recommendation.title: Preserve authenticated delivery
recommendation.body: Redesign pre-authentication admission so invalid traffic remains bounded without consuming the path a valid signed callback must pass, and prove the same-key sequence.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature-introduction and recent merger history makes this person the strongest available owner for the SMS webhook security-versus-delivery policy.
